summary: Edge fanout surge causing api-gateway 5xx elevation and runtime thread-affinity shift for LyraDocs dedicated cluster
description: Issue summary: Beginning ~2026-03-12 09:10 UTC LyraDocs reported elevated 5xx rates from the hosted endpoint routed through our edge fleet. Errors concentrated in the apigw route for streaming chat and long-poll embeddings. Impact: ~92% of LyraDocs requests returned 5xx (502/503) for ~25 minutes, causing production outage for customer processes dependent on low-latency responses. Environment: Dedicated cluster (LyraDocs-dedicated-us-east-1), prod, serving-runtime v1.11.3, api-gateway v2.4.2. Observed behavior: - Sudden fanout of concurrent streaming connections (spike from ~120->6k concurrent streams) - Apigw returned connection resets and 502/503 to upstream for both short and long-lived sessions - Serving runtime logs show thread-affinity migration events and several worker restarts tied to watchdog timeouts - Autoscaler attempted scale-up but experienced oscillation due to warmup GC and prefetch cancellation churn Expected behavior: Apigw should either queue or circuit-break gracefully and serving-runtime should not enter affinity-swap/rest-only restarts that amplify 5xx. Steps to reproduce: 1) Replay LyraDocs traffic pattern in staging using the small-conn-fanout script (attached) 2) Run concurrent streaming sessions with staggered starts to mimic keepalive churn 3) Observe accept queue growth and runtime affinity logs Observed logs/metrics (selected): - Apigw dashboard spike: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/edge/apigw-accept-queue?orgId=1&from=2026-03-12T09:05:00Z - Runtime thread-affinity events: /logs/runtime/lyrad-2026-03-12.log#L2245-L2299 - Watchdog resets correlated to GPU warmup failures: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/runtime/watchdog?from=2026-03-12T09:08:00Z Additional notes: LyraDocs was running a large embedding bulk upload concurrently which likely contributed to KV cache pressure and prefetch invalidations. Customer reported no configuration changes prior to onset.
steps_to_reproduce: Run small-conn-fanout with 6k simulated streaming clients (staggered start) against LyraDocs-dedicated-us-east endpoint
Include a background embedding bulk upload job to reproduce KV/prefetch pressure
Monitor apigw accept-queue, runtime thread-affinity metrics, and autoscaler events
investigation_notes: 09:12 UTC: Support received initial alert and customer screenshots showing streaming resets
09:18 UTC: On-call SRE (Diego) observed accept-queue growth + apigw connection-reset spikes; triaged to serving-runtime after seeing worker thread restart traces
09:28 UTC: Runtime logs show rapid thread-affinity reassignment (affinity-swap) coincident with prefetch invalidation RPCs to kvcache shards
09:35 UTC: Autoscaler attempted two scale-ups; new pods warmed but evicted due to watchdog timeouts on GPU initialization

Hypothesis: Edge fanout surge + large embedding upload caused kvcache lock contention and prefetch cancellations. That triggered synchronous work in runtime that blocked worker loops, causing thread-affinity swaps and eventual watchdog restarts, amplifying 5xx response rate.

Temporary mitigation: Applied per-tenant connection rate limit at apigw (reduced new connections to LyraDocs by ~80%) which flattened the spike. Also disabled concurrent embedding bulk on behalf of customer while remediation proceeds.
Next: add additional telemetry around affinity-swap reasons, adjust autoscaler warmup heuristic, and harden prefetch cancellation handling in runtime.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied 09:45 UTC: per-tenant conn throttle and temporary hold on heavy embedding job — 5xx rate dropped to baseline within ~6 minutes
Planned fix: runtime PR to avoid blocking worker loops on prefetch invalidation (see PR #1227). Also updating autoscaler warmup to account for GPU driver init variance.
Follow-up: postmortem scheduled; add runbook entry for per-tenant fanout protection and clearer fallback to model-variant low-memory path during warmup.
